prompt:
You watch a short video made ONLY of these clips, played back to back with NO narration between them.
Each clip is a person's own words from a show; the shows were not in one conversation. The first clip (label "hook")
opens the video. The hook is shown for context only: it is NOT rated here (its own job was judged on its own).

CLIP label="hook" (on screen: Simply Bitcoin): "Currencies are often born for political reasons, but fail for economic reasons. Bitcoin launched in January of 2009. It's never been renamed. It's never gone into another currency. It's never been redenominated or reissued."
CLIP label="clip_01" (on screen: Stephan Livera): "I think we've seen over time, Bitcoin's volatility has trended lower and lower, effectively making Bitcoin better collateral, because you can borrow more against it and not have to worry about, a 90 % drawdown that we saw, many, many years ago in Bitcoin."
CLIP label="clip_02" (on screen: Robert Breedlove): "So over time, I came to the conclusion that real estate will most likely replace or will be replaced. So real estate will most likely... be replaced by Bitcoin in its function as a savings account."

1) Played back to back with no narration, is there a through-line a viewer can state? State it in ONE sentence, or
   "none" if there is none.
2) For each clip AFTER the hook, rate 1-5 how much it advances that through-line (5 = essential, 1 = off topic).
3) For each JOIN between two consecutive clips, the hook's own join included (does the hook set up the clip after
   it?): could a viewer follow the jump with no narration, i.e. is the next clip's subject or referent clear coming
   from the previous clip's ending? Answer true or false, and why in a few words.
Return ONLY this JSON object: {"through_line": "...", "clips": {"clip_01": 1, "clip_02": 1}, "joins": {"hook -> clip_01": {"followable": true, "why": "..."}, "clip_01 -> clip_02": {"followable": true, "why": "..."}}}
text: {"through_line": "Bitcoin is maturing into a more stable, credible monetary asset that can serve as better collateral and eventually replace traditional savings vehicles like real estate.", "clips": {"clip_01": 4, "clip_02": 4}, "joins": {"hook -> clip_01": {"followable": true, "why": "Bitcoin remains the subject; moves from monetary stability to volatility."}, "clip_01 -> clip_02": {"followable": false, "why": "Abrupt shift from Bitcoin volatility/collateral to real estate savings; no clear referent."}}}
